For a 50-person Indian company, the biggest cost difference is usually not a monthly subscription. It is booking/service fees + airline/hotel cancellation penalties + the amount of human support you need.

MakeMyTrip myBiz	No public fixed subscription fee; service fee is mutually agreed. 1.5% payment-gateway fee can apply to certain wallet/card payments.

OOO
	Supplier-specific. Cleartrip passes supplier refunds through; it doesn't guarantee the underlying travel service.

	24×7 customer support; escalation process available. 
Cleartrip Corporate

FCM Travel	Quote/contract based; likely higher-touch TMC economics rather than a simple free platform.	Changes/cancellations can incur supplier charges up to 100%, plus reissue/service charges; refunds wait for supplier funds. 
FCM Travel
	Contractual service levels should be negotiated; no blanket “warranty” on supplier services.	24×7 emergency assistance, plus travel managers, policy, safety, visa and payment support. 
FCM Travel
+1
What I'd put in the RFQ

For 50 employees, ask each provider for the same 12-month scenario:

150 domestic flight bookings

30 international bookings

150 hotel nights

20 cancellations

15 date changes

10 emergency/after-hours interventions

Then request per-booking fee, cancellation/reissue fee, hotel markup, payment fee, implementation fee and annual minimum, rather than accepting “free platform” as the headline price.

Most important: FCM's published terms explicitly allow cancellation charges of up to 100%, while myBiz and Cleartrip leave the underlying supplier's fare rules controlling.

For India, I’d shortlist these three for a couple wanting medium-firm + a generous home trial:

Wakefit Dual Comfort High Resilience Foam Mattress

4.9

₹14,974•Medium-firm pocket spring mattress for balanced support and comfort.

Give feedback
Pick	Best for	Approx. price*	Trial
Wakefit Dual Comfort	Best value / different firmness preferences	₹7k–₹10k	100 nights
SleepyCat Original	Best balanced medium-firm choice	₹18k–₹21k	100 nights
Wakefit Elevate	Better choice if you want springs + less heat	~₹15k	100 nights

*Prices vary significantly by size/thickness and current offers.

My ranking

1. Wakefit Dual Comfort — best value

Two-sided firmness is useful if you and your partner don't agree on firmness.

Very inexpensive compared with premium options.

Wakefit currently advertises a 100-day home trial across its mattress range. 
Wakefit

Trade-off: basic foam construction, so don't expect the cooling, responsiveness or edge support of a good hybrid/latex mattress.

2. SleepyCat Original — best overall for a couple

Specifically positioned as a medium/medium-firm memory-foam mattress.

100-night trial and 10-year warranty. 
Sleepycat India

Better choice if you want a more conventional "sink in slightly but still supported" feel.

Trade-off: memory foam can sleep warmer and has less bounce than latex or springs.

3. Wakefit Elevate — best if you sleep hot

Pocket-spring + foam construction gives you more airflow, bounce and potentially better movement isolation than basic foam.

Current product results put it around ₹15k depending on size.

Trade-off: more expensive and a spring mattress can feel less uniformly cushioned than all-foam.

One important catch with trials

Buy directly from the manufacturer's website, not Amazon/Flipkart, if the home trial is a major reason you're buying. SleepyCat explicitly says its 100-night trial does not apply to marketplace/quick-commerce purchases. 
Sleepycat India

What I'd check before buying

Actual firmness: Don't rely on "orthopedic." Aim roughly for 6.5–7.5/10 if you both want medium-firm.

Partner disturbance: If one person moves a lot, test motion isolation.

Heat: Memory foam can retain more heat; consider latex/hybrid if either of you sleeps hot.

Edge support: Particularly important on a queen/king used by two adults.

Trial conditions: Check whether you need to sleep on it for a minimum number of days, whether pickup is free, and whether refund/exchange is allowed.

Warranty fine print: A "10-year warranty" doesn't necessarily mean full replacement for 10 years. Coverage can change with age. 
Read This First

Correct size: For two adults, I'd strongly prefer king (72") over queen (60") if your bedroom allows it.

My pick: If you're trying to spend sensibly, Wakefit Dual Comfort. If you're willing to spend ~₹18–21k for a nicer everyday mattress, SleepyCat Original would be my choice.

If you tell me your budget + bed size (queen/king) + whether either of you sleeps hot, I can narrow this to the best 2–3 actual models.
